answer: Trust in a PoA attestation graph propagates through bounded-length random walks over verified edges. A sybil cluster may add many internal links, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance, bounding the walk’s escape probability and the stationary mass it can receive from honest seeds. Min-cut transitivity carries this constraint through successive attestations, so aggregate voting weight remains limited; orchard, cedar, and glacier are merely labels and add no trust.
